proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof, in the setting of Simon 6.2.23 (chapter-06.txt lines 403–412: f_#T needs f|spt T proper; here f = φ is a compactly supported perturbation of the identity), using the inverse function theorem and the mean value inequality; details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P, V := E ∖ K, I := identity of E, ‖·‖ the operator norm.
1. Dφ = I on V. K is compact, hence closed, so V is open. For x ∈ V the map φ agrees with the identity on the neighbourhood V of x, so Dφ(x) = D(id)(x) = I (the Fréchet derivative depends only on the germ: Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
2. φ^{-1}(U) = U. Every point of V is fixed by φ, so φ(V) = V. Since φ is a bijection, φ(K) = φ(E ∖ V) = E ∖ φ(V) = E ∖ V = K. Let x ∈ E. If x ∈ K, then x ∈ U (K ⊆ U) and φ(x) ∈ φ(K) = K ⊆ U, so both x ∈ U and φ(x) ∈ U hold. If x ∉ K, then φ(x) = x. In both cases φ(x) ∈ U ⇔ x ∈ U, i.e. φ^{-1}(U) = U.
3. φ is Λ₁-Lipschitz. Dφ is continuous because φ is C¹ (Mathlib ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). The continuous function x ↦ ‖Dφ(x)‖ is bounded on the compact set K by some c₁ ≥ 0 (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; any c₁ ≥ 0 works if K = ∅). With Λ₁ := max(1, c₁) ∈ ℝ≥0 we get ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ₁ for every x ∈ E, by step 1 off K (‖I‖ ≤ 1). φ is differentiable on the convex set E, so the mean value inequality (Mathlib lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le) shows that φ is Λ₁-Lipschitz.
4. φ is a homeomorphism. φ is continuous. It is proper: for a compact C ⊆ E, φ^{-1}(C) is closed (C is closed, φ continuous) and φ^{-1}(C) ⊆ C ∪ K (if x ∉ K and φ(x) ∈ C then x = φ(x) ∈ C), a compact set; so φ^{-1}(C) is compact (Mathlib isProperMap_iff_isCompact_preimage). A proper map is closed (Mathlib IsProperMap.isClosedMap). A continuous closed bijection is a homeomorphism (Mathlib Equiv.toHomeomorphOfContinuousClosed applied to Equiv.ofBijective φ). Let ψ := φ^{-1}; ψ is continuous.
5. ψ is C¹. For every a ∈ E, Dφ(a) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space E, hence a linear isomorphism (Mathlib LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo), hence a continuous linear equivalence f₀'(a) (finite dimension). As φ is C¹, φ has Fréchet derivative f₀'(a) at every a. By the inverse function theorem for homeomorphisms (Mathlib Homeomorph.contDiff_symm, applied to the homeomorphism of step 4 and f₀'), ψ is C¹.
6. Dψ = I on V and ψ is Λ₂-Lipschitz. For y ∈ V we have φ(y) = y, hence ψ(y) = y; so ψ agrees with the identity on the open set V and, as in step 1, Dψ(y) = I for y ∈ V. Dψ is continuous (ψ is C¹), so ‖Dψ‖ ≤ c₂ on K for some c₂ ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn), and with Λ₂ := max(1, c₂) we get ‖Dψ(y)‖ ≤ Λ₂ for all y ∈ E. By the mean value inequality, ψ is Λ₂-Lipschitz.
7. φ is Λ₂-antilipschitz. For x, y ∈ E: |x − y| = |ψ(φ(x)) − ψ(φ(y))| ≤ Λ₂|φ(x) − φ(y)| (in extended distances: edist x y ≤ Λ₂ · edist (φ x) (φ y)).
8. Conclusion. Put Λ := max(Λ₁, Λ₂) ∈ ℝ≥0. A Λ₁-Lipschitz map is Λ-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.weaken) and a Λ₂-antilipschitz map is Λ-antilipschitz (enlarge the constant in the inequality of step 7). Together with step 2 this gives LipschitzWith Λ φ, AntilipschitzWith Λ φ and φ^{-1}(U) = U. (For P = 0 every step is trivially valid: E is a single point.)
key_steps: Dφ = I on the open set E ∖ K because φ = id there.
φ fixes E ∖ K pointwise and is bijective, so φ(K) = K and φ^{-1}(U) = U.
‖Dφ‖ is bounded (continuous on compact K, ‖I‖ ≤ 1 off K); the mean value inequality makes φ Lipschitz.
φ is proper (φ^{-1}(C) ⊆ C ∪ K), hence closed, hence a homeomorphism.
Homeomorph.contDiff_symm with Dφ(a) a continuous linear equivalence makes ψ = φ^{-1} C¹.
ψ = id off K, so ‖Dψ‖ is bounded and ψ is Lipschitz, i.e. φ is antilipschitz; take Λ the larger constant.
